## Parent

#1

Follow the agent protocol in the parent issue (standing loop, guardrails G1–G8, evidence pack, review, merge gate).

## UI gate (mandatory — this slice ships user-visible UI)

Run the **`impeccable`** skill exactly as its SKILL.md requires: `impeccable context` first, then the matching playbook (`reference/operate.md` for app UI, `reference/new-work.md` for a new surface), and read `reference/craft-floor.md` **before any UI edit** — its craft floor is acceptance criteria, not guidance (contrast, real depth, spacing rhythm, type scale and measure, one authored motion moment, every state including hover/disabled/loading/error/empty, themed browser surfaces, product-language copy). Then run an adversarial **taste pass** (`impeccable critique` and/or the `/design-review` skill) on the rendered result and record findings and fixes in the PR. Verify in a real browser at ~360px / 768px / 1440px plus a keyboard-only pass and `prefers-reduced-motion`, with screenshots attached. Design authority is `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` + `PRODUCT.md`; `mockup/` is reference evidence for interaction and density only — never code to copy.

## What to build

The third lifecycle (D32 layer 2): an Agent's Pi session as a **supervised, on-demand child process** that can be warm, idle-hibernated, crashed, and reconstructed — never the owner of durable data.

- Pi adapter per the #4 decision: one session process per Agent, started on demand when that Agent is addressed; not started at container boot.
- **Warm reuse** while actively used; **idle hibernation** after a configurable timeout, with the durable state intact and the next message transparently restarting the session.
- **Reconstruction from durable state**: a restarted or hibernated session rebuilds its context from SQLite + the pack profile — it must not depend on process memory.
- **Heartbeat-based health**: hung processes are detected (heartbeat window) and distinguished from slow-but-healthy ones; crash → supervised restart with a recorded event; protocol violations (invalid messages from the child) are recorded as protocol failures and never silently dropped (D14).
- **Presence in the UI**: the chat header shows session-active vs hibernating honestly (on-demand session, D32), including a first-time subtle note.
- Session logs are for operators and are redacted (G3); they are never the source of truth for conversations.

## Decisions and specs

- D32 (three lifecycles + policy rules), D14 (JSONL protocol, heartbeats, process-tree termination, fake Pi for tests), D13 (validated seam), D15 (context compiler budget: the session receives compact context, not raw history), D10 (no direct SQL from agent processes), PRD §6, `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` S3 header.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A session starts on demand when the Agent is first addressed; start latency is measured and recorded (no session exists before that).
- [ ] Idle hibernation occurs at the configured timeout; the next message restarts transparently and the conversation continues correctly.
- [ ] Killing the session process mid-conversation loses no durable data; the next message works (test).
- [ ] A hung session (no heartbeat) is detected within the heartbeat window and restarted; a slow-but-healthy session is not killed (scripted test with the fake Pi).
- [ ] An invalid protocol message from the child is recorded as a protocol failure event and the protocol version is enforced.
- [ ] The session process owns no durable state: a test proves the conversation reconstructs correctly with the session process's local state deleted.
- [ ] Process tree termination works for the session (no orphans) — the full cancellation semantics arrive in a later slice.
- [ ] Presence state in the chat header matches reality (asserted against the runtime state, not a fixture).

## Blocked by

- #4
- #12


## Open-source leverage (recorded 2026-09-18)

- **Pattern (primary, MIT):** OpenClaw session lifecycle — repo https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw, search src/ for "idle", "hibernat", "respawn", "session"; docs Gateway section at https://docs.openclaw.ai/. Warm start, idle teardown, and durable-state reconstruction are exactly this slice's problem set, already solved there.
- **Reference:** pi-mono (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) session docs for what inputs a pi session needs on reconstruction.
- **Embed:** none new (node child_process + better-sqlite3 from S03).
